metaDescription: Budget throw pillow inserts for sofas and beds, compared on size, fill, firmness and washability, with plain advice on covers, sizing and flat pillows.
expertTake: The MIULEE 18 inch four-pack is the best overall pick for a sofa because it combines a brushed fabric shell with a firm virgin-fibre fill. The EDOW two-pack is the best value for a first set. Skip the lightest inserts if you want a plump, styled look, because a pillow that weighs less than a pound tends to flatten.
introParagraphs: The cheapest way to refresh a sofa is to change the pillow covers, and the part that decides whether the result looks styled or tired is the insert inside. A good insert fills the corners of the cover and springs back after a lean. A poor one flattens into a pancake within weeks.

This guide covers budget throw pillow inserts, the plain polyester-filled forms that go inside a cover. We focus on the lower half of the price range and on what actually separates them: fill weight, firmness, shell fabric and whether you can wash them. We also explain the sizing trick that makes a cheap pillow look expensive.

products.name: MIULEE 18x18 Pillow Inserts, 4 Pack, virgin fibre fill, 110 GSM brushed shell
products.description:
This four-pack is built around two stated specs that most budget inserts leave out: a 100 percent virgin fibre fill and a brushed shell of 110 grams per square metre. The shell weight matters because very thin covers let fibre clumps show through and allow the fill to migrate. The listing describes the support as firm and flexible, which suits sofa pillows that are leaned on daily.

The tradeoff is that a firm insert looks plump but feels less cuddly than a soft down alternative. Compared with the EDOW two-pack, the MIULEE gives you four inserts and a better-described shell, but you have no weight figure to check against. Four pillows also suit a standard sofa better than two, which can look sparse.

Unpack them a day before you use them, so they can expand, and then fluff and shake each insert. Slip them into covers that are one to two inches smaller than the insert for a full look. Keep them away from damp, since polyester fill dries slowly. If the covers you own have a tight zip, push the insert in one corner at a time and pinch the opposite corner to the cover's corner before closing it.
products.bestFor: Dressing a full sofa with four matching, plump pillows.
pros: Four inserts cover a standard sofa and an accent chair
Virgin fibre fill is stated, with a firm and flexible feel
110 GSM brushed shell hides the fill and feels soft
Standard 18 inch size suits the most common covers
cons: No weight per insert is given, so fullness is unknown
Firm feel is plump but less cuddly than a soft fill

products.name: EDOW Throw Pillow Inserts, Set of 2, 18x18, polyester fibre, 0.99 lb each
products.description:
This is a simple, low-cost pair of 18 by 18 inch inserts with a stated weight of 0.99 pounds each, which is a useful number: it tells you how much fibre is actually inside. The fill is 100 percent polyester fibre with medium support, and the listing says the pillows are gentle-cycle machine washable and can be dried in a dryer or in sunlight to restore their shape.

The compromise is volume. Two inserts are enough for a loveseat or a bed, but a full sofa needs more. Compared with the lighter 0.66 pound EDOW single, this one is noticeably fuller, and compared with the MIULEE it has less shell detail. For a first set, it is hard to beat for cost.

Wash with a mild detergent on a gentle cycle, then tumble on low with a couple of clean tennis balls to break up clumps. Do not skip the final shake and fluff, since fill that dries in a lump will stay lumpy. Store spare inserts in a breathable bag, not vacuum sealed, because long compression leaves permanent creases in polyester fibre.
products.bestFor: A loveseat or bed where two inserts are enough.
pros: Stated 0.99 pound weight shows how much fill is inside
Gentle machine washable, per the listing
Low cost for a pair, and a good first set
Medium support suits both leaning and decoration
cons: Only two inserts, so a full sofa needs another set
Polyester fill can clump if not fluffed after washing

products.name: MIULEE 18x18 Throw Pillow Inserts, 2 Pack, virgin fill, brushed fabric
products.description:
This is the two-pack version of the MIULEE four-pack, with the same virgin microfibre fill and 110 GSM brushed shell. It is the budget-friendly way to test the brand before committing to a set of four. The listing says the fill rebounds and the shell is designed to look and feel good.

The compromise is that it is the same product as the four-pack in a smaller quantity, so it only makes sense if two pillows is all you need. Compared with the EDOW two-pack, it states the shell weight and fill type more clearly, and the price position is similar. Bedrooms and window seats are good uses.

Set the pair in matching covers at each end of a loveseat or bed. Plump them with a karate chop in the top edge for a styled look. The brushed shell can attract lint and pet hair, so keep a lint roller handy. Mixing this pair with a different brand on the same sofa is fine as long as the sizes match, since the shell is hidden by the cover.
products.bestFor: A pair of pillows for a loveseat, bed or window seat.
pros: Same fill and shell as the four-pack, in a smaller set
Third cheapest of nine in the data set, a low-risk entry
110 GSM shell resists fibre migration and lumps
Rebounding fill keeps shape after a lean
cons: A pair will not fill a full sofa
Brushed shell collects lint and pet hair

products.name: Calibrate Timing 18x18 Pillow Inserts, Set of 4, hypoallergenic microfibre
products.description:
This four-pack of 18 by 18 inch inserts uses a hypoallergenic fill and a brushed microfibre liner that the listing says maintains loft and shape. It is described as soft and supportive, with a balance of plush and firm. The set of four works for a sofa with two end pillows and two accent pillows.

The tradeoff is that hypoallergenic describes the material, not a medical claim, and polyester fills do not trap allergens the way a washable sheet might. Compared with the MIULEE four-pack, the specs are less detailed, with no shell weight and no weight per insert. It is a fair mid-range pick when you are mixing brands for different pillows.

Before use, give the inserts a day to expand and shake. Wash covers regularly and the inserts every few months, since the insert holds dust over time. A zipped cover protects the insert from spills better than an envelope cover. If you want a plumper result, open a seam on a spare insert and add a handful of its fibre to this one, then stitch the seam closed.
products.bestFor: A full sofa set where you want a plush but supportive insert.
pros: Four inserts at a mid-low cost fill a standard sofa
Hypoallergenic fill is stated in the listing
Plush yet firm feel works for sofas and beds
Brushed microfibre liner keeps fill inside
cons: Listing gives no fill weight or shell GSM

products.name: EDOW Throw Pillow Insert, 18x18, lightweight polyester, 0.66 lb
products.description:
This is the cheapest insert in the group, a single 18 by 18 inch pillow weighing 0.66 pounds, or about 300 grams. The microfibre fill has medium support, and the listing says it can be gently machine washed and dried to recover its shape. It is a sensible way to replace one flat pillow without buying a set.

The weakness is that weight. At 0.66 pounds, it is lighter than the 0.99 pound EDOW pair, so it will look flatter and more relaxed in a cover. If you want a crisp, plump look, choose a fuller insert, or stuff a cover with a smaller insert for a lounge look instead.

Use it where you want a soft, casual pillow, such as on a bed. In a sofa corner, pair it with a cover that is a size down from the insert so the corners fill. After washing, add a small handful of extra fibre if the pillow still looks flat. Use it in a cover with a heavy fabric such as linen or velvet, which holds the shape better than a thin cotton cover.
products.bestFor: Replacing a single flat pillow or a casual bed pillow at the lowest cost.
pros: Lowest cost for a single insert in the guide
Stated weight lets you judge fullness before you buy
Washable, per the listing, and quick to refresh
18 inch size fits the most common covers
cons: Lightest insert here, so it looks flatter than the others
Sold as a single, so sets cost more per pillow

buyingCriteria.explanation: A plump look comes from an insert that is one to two inches larger than the cover. An 18 inch insert in a 16 inch cover fills the corners, while an 18 inch insert in an 18 inch cover looks floppy. Buyers often match sizes exactly and then wonder why the pillow looks flat. A tape measure beats the listing: measure the cover seam to seam on a flat surface, then add one to two inches for the insert.

Weight is the best budget proxy for fullness. The EDOW pair lists 0.99 pounds each and the single lists 0.66, so the pair is about half again as full. A pillow under a pound will flatten faster, while one near a pound and a half holds a firm shape. Pick up two inserts of different weight if you can, and compare how each holds a shape after you press a fist into it for ten seconds.

A firm insert, like the MIULEE, looks neat and supports your back for a few minutes. A soft insert is more comfortable for a long lean but looks rumpled. Choose firm for display and soft for real use. Reading the shell description matters because thin liners are the commonest reason cheap inserts clump and show lumps through the cover.

A brushed shell of 110 GSM, as on the MIULEE, hides the fill and resists lumps. A very thin shell lets fibre migrate and clump. Cheap inserts often have a see-through liner, so a heavier shell is a quiet sign of quality. Keep inserts away from damp rooms and open windows during rain, since polyester stays damp inside and can develop a stale smell.

Most polyester inserts can be machine washed on gentle, but they need a slow, low-heat dry and a good fluff. Washing too often breaks down the fibre and makes it clump. Wash covers monthly and inserts a few times a year. Test one insert before ordering a second set so you know the firmness suits your sofa before you commit to the full number.

Buying a four-pack lowers the cost per pillow, but only if you will use all four. A sofa needs three to five, and a bed two to four. Count the pillows you actually plan to style before buying. Buy in sets when styling an entire sofa, but buy a single when you only need a replacement for the one pillow that went flat.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fullness and size
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each insert on stated size and fill weight. The EDOW pair at 0.99 pounds is the only one with a clear weight alongside the single at 0.66. We worked from published specifications. We read each listing for what it leaves out, such as missing weight or shell details.

howWeEvaluated.title: Shell and construction
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared shell descriptions. The MIULEE lists a 110 GSM brushed shell, and the others are less detailed. Shell weight affects clumping and lint. We treated down alternative wording as polyester fibre, because the listings describe the fill that way.

howWeEvaluated.title: Washing instructions
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the stated care. The EDOW lists a gentle machine wash, and the others imply it. Owner feedback patterns often mention clumping after washing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Set size and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at pack sizes. The four-packs lower the cost per pillow, and the single is the cheapest overall. We do not publish ratings or review counts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: None of these are down or feather inserts. Polyester fibre flattens over time, and every one of them will eventually need replacing. We say so.

maintenance.why: Fill compacts with use. A shake and a karate chop restore shape. Do it while watching television so the habit sticks.
Covers take the dirt. Wash according to the label. Spot clean any spill on the cover before it soaks into the insert, where stains are hard to remove.
Inserts hold dust and oils. Use a gentle cycle and dry on low with tennis balls.
Pillows at the end of the sofa get more use. Swapping them evens the wear.
Polyester fibre breaks down. A flat insert will not recover with washing.

faq.q: What size insert should I buy for a cover?
faq.a: Choose an insert one to two inches larger than the cover, such as an 18 inch insert in a 16 inch cover, for a plump look. For a very plump look, pair an insert with a cover that is two inches smaller.
Most polyester inserts can be gently machine washed. Dry on low with a few clean tennis balls and fluff afterward. If a washed insert smells musty, air it in dry sunlight for a few hours.

faq.q: Are polyester inserts as good as down?
faq.a: They are cheaper and washable but less airy and they flatten sooner. Down alternatives are fine for decoration. Keep the original packaging if you plan to return a flat insert.

faq.q: How many pillows does a sofa need?
faq.a: Three to five on a standard sofa, odd numbers often look natural. Mix sizes for a styled look.

faq.q: Why is my new insert flat?
faq.a: Compressed shipping flattens it. Give it a day to expand and fluff it well.
Yes, an insert alone looks plain and gets dirty. A cover also protects the shell.
